title_prefix: No RPCHelpMan type gate: wrong-typed arg
mechanism: Core runs one shared gate before any handler body. RPCHelpMan::HandleRequest (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/util.cpp:640-657 at d3056bc) first calls IsValidNumArgs (util.cpp:733-743) and, on a count outside [required, declared], throws HelpResult{ToString()}; ExecuteCommand catches that std::exception and turns it into JSONRPCError(RPC_MISC_ERROR = -1, help text) (rpc/server.cpp:503-518). It then loops over EVERY declared position calling RPCArg::MatchesType (util.cpp:899), collects each failure into an object keyed "Position N (name)", and throws ONE JSONRPCError(RPC_TYPE_ERROR = -3, "Wrong type passed:\n" + that object written with indent 4). Our define-rpc has no type declarations at all: a spec is a variable plus one of six positional COERCIONS (:bool, :bool-or, :array, :or, :integer-or, :string-or) and expands to (destructuring-bind (&optional vars &rest more) params (declare (ignore more)) ...) -- src/rpc/define-rpc.lisp:71-100, the (ignore more) at :91-92 being exactly where a superfluous argument disappears. dispatch-rpc-method (src/rpc/server.lisp:68-86) checks warmup and method existence and then funcalls the handler; it performs no arity or type check. The -3 replies we do produce come from per-handler calls to %json-type-error (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:231-244) and node.lisp:60, which emit only the inner sentence for the FIRST offending position.
consequence: Wrong-typed arguments come back with the wrong error class and, for most methods, a hand-written -8 sentence, so a client cannot tell 'this is not a number' from 'this number is out of range'; and a call with too many or too few arguments is not refused at all. Executed at the wire: getblockhash("foo") and getblockhash(true) and getblockhash(1.5) all answer -8 "Invalid height parameter" where Core answers -3 with the Wrong-type object; estimatesmartfee("6") answers -8 "Invalid conf_target, must be between 1 and 1008"; gettxout(txid,"x") answers -8 "Invalid txid"; getrawtransaction("aa",[]) answers -8 "Invalid transaction id". getnetworkhashps("a",[]) does answer -3 but with only "JSON value of type string is not of expected type number" -- no "Wrong type passed:" wrapper and no Position 2 entry, where rpc_blockchain.py:496-506 asserts the full two-position text verbatim. Arity: getblockcount(1,2,3) and uptime(1,2,3) both SUCCEED; getchaintxstats(0,"",0) answers -5 "Block not found" where rpc_blockchain.py:311 asserts -1 'getchaintxstats'; prioritisetransaction() and prioritisetransaction("",0,0,0) both answer -8 "Invalid txid" where mining_prioritisetransaction.py:206-211 asserts -1 'prioritisetransaction'; help("foo","bar") returns the string "help: unknown command: foo" where rpc_help.py:126 asserts -1 'help'; help(0) returns the WHOLE command listing where rpc_help.py:130 asserts -3 "JSON value of type number is not of expected type string". Held at S3 rather than S2: every divergence needs the client to send an argument Core would have rejected, no correct call returns a wrong value, and the one place where ignoring an argument does change a returned value -- createrawtransaction dropping replaceable and version -- is already filed separately as fa699133 (S2). A reader who counts help(0) answering 200 OK with a full listing, instead of -3, as a behaviour change could re-grade this to S2.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3c, warm image (scripts/dev.sh, bitcoin-lisp loaded). Probes probe1.lisp/probe2.lisp/probe3.lisp drove bl.rpc::dispatch-rpc-method over %normalize-rpc-params against a minimal testnet3 node; probe9.lisp/probe10.lisp drove the same calls through bl.rpc::handle-single-request and yason:encode so the reply text is what a client reads. Outputs: getnetworkhashps("a",[]) -> {"error":{"code":-3,"message":"JSON value of type string is not of expected type number"}}; getnetworkhashps(120,[]) -> -3 "...type array is not of expected type number"; getblockhash("foo") -> {"error":{"code":-8,"message":"Invalid height parameter"}}; getblockcount(1,2,3) -> {"result":0}; uptime(1,2,3) -> {"result":0}; help(0) -> {"result":"abandontransaction\nabortrescan\n..."}; help("foo","bar") -> {"result":"help: unknown command: foo"}; getchaintxstats(0,"",0) -> -5 "Block not found"; prioritisetransaction("",0,0,0) -> -8 "Invalid txid". Tree grep: `grep -rn "Wrong type passed" src/ tests/` returns nothing (the only hits for the inner sentence are src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:243, src/rpc/node.lisp:60 and their tests). Ours: src/rpc/define-rpc.lisp:71-100 (the coercion table and the (declare (ignore more))), src/rpc/server.lisp:68-86. Core at d3056bc: rpc/util.cpp:640-657 (HandleRequest), :733-743 (IsValidNumArgs), :899-910 (MatchesType), rpc/server.cpp:503-518 (HelpResult -> RPC_MISC_ERROR). Core functional tests: rpc_blockchain.py:496-506 and :311, rpc_help.py:126 and :130, mining_prioritisetransaction.py:206-214.
fix_shape: Give define-rpc the declared type Core's RPCArg carries, and enforce it in one place before the handler body runs. Extend the positional spec so each position names its Core RPCArg::Type (num, str, bool, arr, obj, str_hex, amount) and whether it is required, keeping the existing coercion keywords as the post-check step; then have dispatch-rpc-method (or the define-rpc prologue, so the check is generated once per method rather than written per handler) do exactly what HandleRequest does in exactly that order: reject a parameter count outside [required, declared] with +rpc-misc-error+ (-1) and the method's help text, then walk EVERY declared position, collect each mismatch as "Position N (name)" -> the existing %json-type-error sentence, and if the collection is non-empty signal one +rpc-type-error+ (-3) whose message is "Wrong type passed:\n" followed by that object serialized with yason at indent 4 so the text matches rpc_blockchain.py byte for byte. Null must stay accepted everywhere (Core's VNULL case) and the +json-false+ / +json-empty-array+ sentinels must be classified as bool and arr, not as truthy atoms. Once the gate exists, the per-handler -8 sentences it subsumes ('Invalid height parameter' for a non-number, 'Invalid txid' for a non-string) should be deleted rather than left as unreachable second checks, and the range checks that share those messages kept. A regression test should assert the exact two-position getnetworkhashps text and one -1 arity reply.
